cosmic_rain.status: REJECTED by user 2026-10-27 after viewing: weird, not symmetrical, not interesting, develops far too slowly. Not flickering and continuous, but the chained Wan last-frame approach is the wrong method for the Ayana target. Keep the file as a reference only; do not extend, upscale or re-finish it.
cosmic_rain.rejection_diagnosis: Ayana reference (sampled 20-340s): bold illustrated psytrance poster style, one readable subject per scene, centred or bilaterally symmetric compositions (spiral tunnel, eye, mushroom forest, rows of identical jellyfish/characters/dancing skeletons), constant camera motion from the start, clean scene changes every few seconds. Pilot: photoreal cosmic look, ~30s of near-still frames, chained morph drift turning subjects into odd things, symmetry only as 3 brief accents.
cosmic_rain.proposed_next: Keyframe-first: storyboard ~20 scenes of 2-4 bars, generate stills on the idle A2000 with existing local models (mirror-symmetric where the scene calls for it), user approves stills, then animate each from its own keyframe (not chained) with cuts/portals on bar lines. Awaiting user go-ahead and style decision.

cosmic_rain.gemini_ayana_analysis: User gave Codex a Gemini breakdown of Ayana before the pilot: modular 1-bar/2-bar I2V clips, hard cuts on bar 1, eye/circle portal match-zooms, 2D mirror/radial/clone compositing, reverse-timed impacts, acts. The pilot applied the cut grid but not the compositing, fresh-keyframe-per-clip or portals, and chained last frames (the drift Gemini warned against). Gemini's '40 frames per bar at 24fps' drifts (bar is 40.28 frames); use absolute timestamps. Its timestamps are partly wrong against sampled frames; its waveform brightness pulses conflict with the no-strobe preference; Flow/Veo are paid and excluded.
